newsitem.title: USA: Teamsters' Carey says will launch organizing push.
newsitem.headline: Teamsters' Carey says will launch organizing push.

text.p: The Teamsters Union will train 10,000 volunteers and build a core of 1,000 full-time local organizers "to organize on a scale like never before," Ron Carey, the newly re-elected union president, said Tuesday.

With his inauguration slated for Saturday, Carey said in a telephone news conference, "That's where those key goals will be going to, to spread our smart strategies to every local union, to organize on a scale like never before."

Carey, who narrowly defeated James Hoffa to lead the 1.4 million-member union, also said he had sent action plans to locals on their role in building union membership, which he said had held steady over the last two years.
He said he did not expect the organizing push to be expensive as it would be done mostly through volunteers.
"We have our own organizing department ... and that will be the start and from there move in the direction of a volunteer organizer approach," Carey said.
Carey also said the Teamsters have had "exploratory" talks with other unions on possible mergers.

"We are in the process of talking to a number of different individuals who have shown some interest and who believe the Teamsters Union is the proper place for them to be," he said, but he would not name the organizations.

Carey, who leads a fractious organization after the bitterly contested election against Hoffa, said he expected to get approval this week from a court-appointed election officer so he can be installed as president this weekend.
Hoffa's backers have pushed for a delay in the installation, citing an investigation over a campaign contribution to Carey.
But Carey said he saw no reason to postpone the installation.
"I'm not going to run after his rabbit, obviously. When you look at the amount of money that he has collected there are some real serious question marks about his fundraising as well," Carey said.
